sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for the respondents.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of the residential house in survey No.106-1B1, Bodiganidoddi Village, Bukkarayasamudram Mandal,
Anantapur District.
He further submits that the petitioner's land and the building are situated in 105 Sq. yards in survey No.106-1B1 and the same were acquired by the respondents and paid the compensation.
After acquisition of the said land the petitioner got constructed a house within his private patta land, which is out of the acquired portion by the respondents.

He further submits that even though, the petitioner got constructed in the land, which is out of the acquired portion of the land as well as out of the portion of the Government land, the respondents are threatening for demolition of the land.
Hence, the present Writ petition.

4. On the other hand, learned Government Pleader for the respondents furnished written instructions of the 7th respondent dated 22.06.2024, wherein the respondents categorically admitted as follows:
"In this regard it is submitted that, the land in survey No.106 of Bodiganidoddi Village is only acquired once, as per Award No.14/2019, duly sub-dividing the acquired portion as 106-1B1, ext 0.22 acre and no further acquisitions took place.
Further
, the new house which has been built by the petitioner, adjacent to the acquired portion in survey No.106-1, is not situated in acquired portion and it falls in his private patta.
Only his old house adjacent to the existing road falls in acquired portion.

It is further submitted that an amount of Rs.2,41,500 has been paid as land compensation, and an amount of Rs.33,71,691 has been paid as structure(house)
compensation."

5. Learned Government Pleader for the respondents further submits that the house constructed by the petitioner in survey No.106-1 is not situated within the acquired portion of the respondents for laying road and further admitted that the said portion of the land where the petitioner got constructed house is situated within the private pata of the petitioner.
Therefore, the respondents are neither trying to dispossess nor trying to demolish the construction of the petitioner.

6. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for the respondents, this Court is of the considered view, the present Writ Petition can be disposed of directing the respondents, if they intend to interfere or dispossess the petitioner from the new residential house constructed in his patta land as admitted by the respondents in their written instructions dated 22.06.2024, the respondents are restrained from such interference without following due process of law.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
